neighbours.label: electrical-hazard safety warnings (frayed cords, downed power lines, live wires that can shock or cause outages), read on the word just before the harm, as against the same warnings about non-electrical hazards
fire: Inspect the lamp cord often, and replace it if the insulation is cracked.
Do not plug too many heaters into one outlet, or the wiring may overheat.
Stay at least ten meters away from a fallen power line, since it may still be live.
Unplug the toaster before cleaning it so you are not shocked.
Keep metal ladders clear of overhead lines to avoid electrocution.
Never use a hair dryer near the bath, as water and current can kill.
A damaged extension cable can short out and start a fire in the walls.
Turn off the breaker first, because touching a live wire can stop your heart.
quiet: Inspect the garden hose often, and replace it if the rubber is cracked.
Do not stack too many boxes on one shelf, or the bracket may bend.
Stay at least ten meters away from a fallen tree, since it may still shift.
Let the oven cool before cleaning it so you are not burned.
Keep wooden ladders on firm ground to avoid a bad fall.
Never leave a toddler near the bath, as even shallow water can kill.
A loose roof tile can slide off and hit someone on the path below.
Wear gloves first, because touching a sharp blade can cut your hand.
